title: Setting Up Your AI Coding Environment
description: Get practical guidance on installing and configuring GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and other AI coding tools in your development environment.

data.text: Most AI coding tools require just a supported IDE and an account. The exact requirements depend on the tool, but you typically need a modern IDE (VS Code, JetBrains, or Neovim), a stable internet connection for cloud-based models, and in some cases, a paid subscription for the most capable models.
Setting Up GitHub Copilot in VS Code

data.title: Step-by-step setup:
items: Open VS Code and go to the Extensions view (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+X)
Search for 'GitHub Copilot' and install it
Click 'Sign in to GitHub' when prompted
Choose a Copilot plan: Individual ($10/month), Business ($19/user/month), or free if you qualify
Open a code file and start typing — suggestions should appear

data.title: Enable additional features
data.text: After installing Copilot, enable Copilot Chat and Copilot Edges in the extension settings for the full experience. Inline completions work out of the box, but Chat requires enabling the separate 'GitHub Copilot Chat' extension.

data.title: Installation steps:
items: Download Cursor from cursor.sh or use Homebrew: brew install --cask cursor
Open Cursor and sign in or create an account
Install the Cursor extension pack if migrating from VS Code
Open a project — Cursor will automatically start indexing
Configure your preferred AI model in settings (default is usually fine to start)

data.text: Cursor works as a standalone IDE. It imports your VS Code settings and extensions automatically, making the transition smooth. If you use VS Code settings sync, Cursor can pull your configuration directly.

You do not need every tool to be productive. Most developers start with one primary tool and add others as needed. GitHub Copilot is the safest starting point for VS Code users. Cursor is better if you want the deepest AI integration. Web chat interfaces (ChatGPT, Claude) complement either tool for architecture and debugging.

cards.title: GitHub Copilot + VS Code
cards.description: Best for most developers. Mature, reliable, widely adopted. Great autocomplete and improving chat features.

cards.title: Cursor IDE
cards.description: Best for developers who want AI-first workflows. Deeper codebase awareness, better multi-file editing.

cards.title: Web chat (ChatGPT / Claude)
cards.description: Best as a complement to any IDE tool. Excellent for architecture, debugging, and learning.

data.title: After setup, optimize your experience:
items: Disable inline suggestions in files you do not want AI to read (secrets, generated code)
Configure which file types Copilot should suggest in (enable for your main languages, disable for config files)
Set up keyboard shortcuts for common actions (accept suggestion, open chat, trigger inline edit)
Enable automatic updates but test after each major version update
Consider privacy settings if working with proprietary code

data.text: Verify your setup works by opening a file in a language you know well and starting to type. You should see inline suggestions within a few keystrokes. Try the chat feature by selecting a function and asking for an explanation. If suggestions do not appear, check that the extension is enabled and that your account is authenticated.

data.title: First suggestion checklist
data.text: Your first AI suggestion should feel natural, not magical. If it does not appear within 5 seconds of typing, check the extension status bar. If the extension is active and suggestions are still missing, try restarting your IDE.

data.title: Example: verifying Copilot works
data.content:
1. Open a new TypeScript file
2. Start typing: function calculateTotal(price: number, tax: number)
3. Copilot should suggest the function body
4. Press Tab to accept
5. Open Copilot Chat and select the function
6. Ask: "Add input validation and return a Result type"
7. Verify the AI modifies the function correctly

data.title: Setup checklist
points: Choose a primary tool (Copilot, Cursor, or web chat)
Verify suggestions appear with a test function
